sections.text: This checkpoint practises Unit 5: vectors, String and &str, and HashMap. You will write three functions that split a text into words and count them.
It draws on the lessons Vectors, String and &str and HashMap. HashMap<String, u32> is a map with String keys and u32 values, in the same way as Vec<String> is a list of Strings.

todo!() is a placeholder. If the program reaches it, it stops with the message "not yet implemented". Replace each todo!() with your own code. Until you do, the compiler may warn that some names are unused. That is expected.

Hint for split_words: make an empty vector with let mut words = Vec::new();. Then loop over text.split_whitespace(). It gives the words as &str and ignores extra spaces. word.to_lowercase() makes a new String, which you can push onto the vector.

Hint for word_counts: a HashMap owns its keys, so each key must be a String. In the loop, word is a &String, so give word.clone() to entry. Then use or_insert(0) and add 1, as in the HashMap lesson. The last line gives back the map.
Hint for count_of: get returns an Option that holds a reference to the number. Use unwrap_or(&0) for a missing word, and * to get the number out. get accepts a &str even though the keys are Strings.
A HashMap does not keep its keys in a fixed order. That is why main sorts the keys before it prints them.

exercise.prompt:
Replace each todo!() with working code. Do not change main.

fn split_words(text: &str) -> Vec<String>
Gives back the words of text, in order, each one in lowercase. Words are separated by spaces, and extra spaces are ignored. A text with no words gives an empty Vec.

fn word_counts(words: &[String]) -> HashMap<String, u32>
Gives back a map from each different word to the number of times it appears.

fn count_of(counts: &HashMap<String, u32>, word: &str) -> u32
Gives back how many times word appears in counts, or 0 if it is not there.

The program should print:
8 words
and: 2
cat: 1
end: 1
hat: 1
the: 3
the appears 3 times
dog appears 0 times
[spaced]
[out]
0 words, 0 different

quiz.question: Why does word_counts give word.clone() to entry?
options: clone is needed for every HashMap call
The map owns its keys, but word is only a borrowed reference

quiz.question: What does len() count for a String?
What does counts.get("dog") return when "dog" is not in the map?
